edges.reason: Finding gray_stained_glass locates the glass gallery where light_blue_stained_glass_panes are placed 2 blocks closer to spawn
Finding the glass gallery reveals the crafting table at (~2,0,-9) needed to craft white_stained_glass from player's glass and bone_meal
The green_wall_banner marks the entrance to the nether-themed alcove where weeping_vines hang from the ceiling
Granite blocks form the sealed front wall of the vault room; mining them is the only way to reach the shulker box inside
The shulker box contains 10 iron ingots; 7 are needed to craft a cauldron at the adjacent crafting table
The shulker box is the only source of iron ingots in the scene, needed to trade with the villager merchant
The fully-enclosed terracotta room has no door; mining through the white_terracotta walls is the only way to access the gray_wool inside
Mining gray_wool places the player inside the enclosed room where the leather chest and crafting table are located
The leather chest and crafting table for the helmet are inside the sealed terracotta room, accessible only after mining through the walls

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The gray_stained_glass wall is at spawn-relative (0, 1, -10). Max distance set to 4 blocks to require intentional navigation (player spawns 10 blocks away, must walk ~6 blocks north). Facing tolerance 60° ensures they're looking at the glass wall. WHY this rule: find tasks require the player to visually locate and approach the target.

Uses count_in_box_at_most because light_blue_stained_glass_pane shatters without Silk Touch and drops nothing — inventory_has cannot be used. 4 panes are placed at z=-8, x=-2 to 1, y=1. max_count=3 means at least 1 must be destroyed (singular 'mine' task). WHY this rule: the only way to detect mining of a block that drops nothing is to verify the block is no longer present.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The green_wall_banner is at spawn-relative (7, 2, 0) facing west. Max distance set to 4 blocks to require intentional navigation (player spawns ~7 blocks away, must walk east). Facing tolerance 60° ensures they're looking at the banner. WHY this rule: find tasks require the player to visually locate and approach the target.

Uses inventory_has because weeping vines drop themselves as items when broken with shears (player has shears in starting inventory). WHY this rule: mine tasks where the block drops an item are best verified by checking inventory for the dropped item.

Uses inventory_has because white terracotta drops itself when mined with a pickaxe (player has diamond pickaxe). The terracotta room is fully sealed — mining through the wall is the only way in. WHY this rule: mine tasks where the block drops an item are best verified by checking inventory.

Uses inventory_has because gray wool drops itself when mined (any tool works, shears are fastest). The wool is inside the sealed terracotta room, accessible only after mining through terracotta walls. WHY this rule: mine tasks where the block drops an item are best verified by checking inventory.

Uses inventory_has because the crafted leather_helmet ends up in inventory. Recipe: 5 leather in helmet pattern at crafting table inside the terracotta room. Leather source: chest at (~-8, 0, 1) with 5 leather. WHY this rule: craft tasks always produce an item that appears in inventory.

Uses inventory_has because granite drops itself when mined with a pickaxe (player has diamond pickaxe). The granite front wall (z=8, x=-2 to 4, y=0-2) is the ONLY entry to the sealed vault room containing the shulker box. WHY this rule: mine tasks where the block drops an item are best verified by checking inventory.

Uses inventory_has because the shulker box at (~1, 0, 11) is the ONLY source of iron ingots in the scene. Having iron_ingot in inventory confirms the box was opened and items were taken. WHY this rule: there is no direct 'open container' event, so we verify the unique contents appeared in inventory as proof of interaction.

Uses inventory_has because the crafted cauldron ends up in inventory. Recipe: 7 iron ingots in U-shape at crafting table (~3, 0, 11) inside the vault. Iron ingots sourced from shulker box (10 available). WHY this rule: craft tasks always produce an item that appears in inventory.

Uses inventory_has because crafted white_stained_glass ends up in inventory. Requires two crafting steps: (1) bone_meal → white_dye, (2) 8 glass + 1 white_dye → 8 white_stained_glass. Player starts with 8 glass and 4 bone_meal. Crafting table at (~2, 0, -9). WHY this rule: craft tasks always produce an item that appears in inventory.

Uses inventory_has because the villager trade (1 iron_ingot → 1 emerald) produces an emerald that ends up in inventory. No other emerald source exists in the scene, so having an emerald confirms a successful sale to the toolsmith villager at (~0, 0, 12). WHY this rule: trade/sell tasks produce a unique item (emerald) that serves as proof of transaction.

scene_description: A compact multi-room workshop compound centered around the player spawn. Four distinct areas radiate outward: (1) North - Glass Gallery with gray_stained_glass windows and light_blue_stained_glass_panes plus crafting table. (2) East - Nether alcove marked by green_wall_banner with weeping_vines hanging from nether brick ceiling. (3) South - Fully sealed stone brick vault with granite front wall as the ONLY entry, containing shulker box (10 iron ingots), crafting table, and villager merchant. (4) West - Fully sealed white terracotta room (all walls y=0-2 + ceiling) containing gray_wool, leather chest, and crafting table. Both sealed rooms have NO alternative entry points, physically enforcing the dependency graph.
task_text: Explore the artisan workshop compound. Find the gray stained glass in the north gallery, then mine the light blue stained glass panes and craft white stained glass. Locate the green wall banner marking the nether alcove and mine the weeping vines. In the west wing, mine through the white terracotta wall to access and mine gray wool, then craft a leather helmet using leather from the chest inside. In the south vault, mine through the granite wall to reach and open the shulker box containing iron ingots. Use those ingots to craft a cauldron, then sell an iron ingot to the villager merchant inside the vault.
design_notes: FINAL APPROVED DESIGN. Layout from player spawn at (0,0,0): NORTH (z=-8 to -10): Glass gallery - gray_stained_glass wall at z=-10 (2 rows of 5), light_blue_stained_glass_panes at z=-8 (row of 4 at eye level), crafting table at (~2,0,-9). EAST (x=7-11): Nether alcove - nether brick structure with floor and ceiling, green_wall_banner at (~7,2,0) facing west (visible from approach), weeping_vines hanging from ceiling. SOUTH (z=8-13): SEALED vault room - granite front wall at z=8 (7 blocks wide × 3 tall, x=-2 to 4, y=0-2), stone_brick side walls (x=-2, x=4), back wall (z=13), and ceiling (y=3). Interior contains: shulker box at (~1,0,11) with 10 iron ingots, crafting table at (~3,0,11), NoAI villager at (~0,0,12) with iron→emerald trade. WEST (x=-7 to -11): SEALED terracotta room - ALL four walls at full height (y=0-2) plus ceiling (y=3). East wall at x=-7, west wall at x=-11, north wall at z=-2, south wall at z=2. Interior contains: gray_wool (4 blocks at x=-9/-10, y=0-1, z=0), crafting table at (~-8,0,0), chest with 5 leather at (~-8,0,1). Player inventory: diamond_pickaxe, shears, bone_meal×4, glass×8. Target MC version: 1.14-1.20.4.
